motions.item_title: Decision Report 115 Watson Parkway North Proposed Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision, 2026-134
motions.text: That the application from Zelinka Priamo Ltd., on behalf of the owner, Guelph Watson Holdings Inc. for a Zoning By-law Amendment to change the zoning from the “Site-specific Commercial Mixed-Use Centre with a Parking Adjustment Suffix and Holding Provisions” (CMUC-9(PA)(H10)(H12)) Zone, to an amended “Site-specific Commercial Mixed-Use Centre with a Parking Adjustment Suffix and Holding Provisions” (CMUC-9(PA)(H)) Zone, to the “Neighbourhood Park” (NP) Zone, to modify the boundaries of the “Natural Heritage Sytstem” (NHS) Zone, and to modify the Floodplain (FL) Overlay, according to Zoning By-law (2023)-20790, as amended, to permit the development of four mixed use buildings ranging in height from nine (9) to fourteen (14) storeys, consisting of approximately 928 dwelling units and 2,750 square metres of at-grade commercial space, 31 on-street townhouse units, 170 back-to-back townhouse units (approximately 1,129 dwelling units in total), on the property municipally known as 115 Watson Parkway North and legally described as Part of Lot 5, Concession 3, Division C, City of Guelph, be approved in accordance with recommended zoning regulations in Attachment-3 and zoning mapping in Attachment-7 of Infrastructure, Development and Environment report dated May 12, 2026. That in accordance with Section 34(17) of the Planning Act, City Council has determined that no further public notice is required related to the proposed Zoning By-law Amendment affecting 115 Watson Parkway North. That the application from Zelinka Priamo Ltd., on behalf of the owner, Guelph Watson Holdings Inc. for approval of a Draft Plan of Subdivision consisting of two (2) Commercial Mixed-use Centre Blocks, one (1) Multiple Residential Block, one (1) Natural Heritage System Block and one (1) Neighbourhood Park Block, and four (4), 0.3 metre Reserve Blocks as shown in Attachment-10, on the property municipally known as 115 Watson Parkway North and legally described as Part of Lot 5, Concession 3, Division C, City of Guelph, be approved for three (3) years in accordance with draft plan conditions outlined in Attachment-4 Recommended Draft Plan Conditions of Infrastructure, Development and Environment report dated May 12, 2026.
motions.text_html:
1. That the application from Zelinka Priamo Ltd., on behalf of the owner, Guelph Watson Holdings Inc. for a Zoning By-law Amendment to change the zoning from the “Site-specific Commercial Mixed-Use Centre with a Parking Adjustment Suffix and Holding Provisions” (CMUC-9(PA)(H10)(H12)) Zone, to an amended “Site-specific Commercial Mixed-Use Centre with a Parking Adjustment Suffix and Holding Provisions” (CMUC-9(PA)(H)) Zone, to the “Neighbourhood Park” (NP) Zone, to modify the boundaries of the “Natural Heritage Sytstem” (NHS) Zone, and to modify the Floodplain (FL) Overlay, according to Zoning By-law (2023)-20790, as amended, to permit the development of four mixed use buildings ranging in height from nine (9) to fourteen (14) storeys, consisting of approximately 928 dwelling units and 2,750 square metres of at-grade commercial space, 31 on-street townhouse units, 170 back-to-back townhouse units (approximately 1,129 dwelling units in total), on the property municipally known as 115 Watson Parkway North and legally described as Part of Lot 5, Concession 3, Division C, City of Guelph, be approved in accordance with recommended zoning regulations in Attachment-3 and zoning mapping in Attachment-7 of Infrastructure, Development and Environment report dated May 12, 2026.
  2. That in accordance with Section 34(17) of the Planning Act, City Council has determined that no further public notice is required related to the proposed Zoning By-law Amendment affecting 115 Watson Parkway North.
  3. That the application from Zelinka Priamo Ltd., on behalf of the owner, Guelph Watson Holdings Inc. for approval of a Draft Plan of Subdivision consisting of two (2) Commercial Mixed-use Centre Blocks, one (1) Multiple Residential Block, one (1) Natural Heritage System Block and one (1) Neighbourhood Park Block, and four (4), 0.3 metre Reserve Blocks as shown in Attachment-10, on the property municipally known as 115 Watson Parkway North and legally described as Part of Lot 5, Concession 3, Division C, City of Guelph, be approved for three (3) years in accordance with draft plan conditions outlined in Attachment-4 Recommended Draft Plan Conditions of Infrastructure, Development and Environment report dated May 12, 2026.

motions.item_title: Decision Report for Proposed Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 328 Victoria Road South and 588 Stone Road East (also referred to as the Guelph Innovation District (GID) Block 1 and 2 lands), 2026-185
motions.name: Main Motion
motions.text: That Council defer its decision and direct staff to continue to work collaboratively with the applicant to address the outstanding policy, technical, and regulatory matters identified in this report. Recognizing that this is one of the City’s key growth areas and provides employment and residential growth to 2051, that staff report back to Council in September provided the applicant provides updated supportable material by June 15, 2026, with an updated analysis and recommendation should the outstanding matters be satisfactorily resolved.

motions.item_title: Exploring the Potential for Five Plus (5+) Units in Guelph, 2026-229
motions.name: First Motion
motions.text: That Council direct staff to continue evaluating the feasibility of permitting five or more residential units with the approach presented on low density residential corner lots (RL.1 and RL.2), and to undertake the following actions: That the review of five plus units exclude corner lots strictly at the intersection of arterial and collector roads; That the review of five plus units focus on corner lots that meet the criteria at the intersection of: arterial or collector and local roads; and, two local roads. Prepare draft Official Plan policies and a zoning by-law amendment, as necessary, to support the implementation of five or more residential units per lot; and Report back to Council in 2027 with findings, proposed policy directions, and recommended regulatory changes for consideration.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council direct staff to continue evaluating the feasibility of permitting five or more residential units with the approach presented on low density residential corner lots (RL.1 and RL.2), and to undertake the following actions:
    1. That the review of five plus units exclude corner lots strictly at the intersection of arterial and collector roads;
    2. That the review of five plus units focus on corner lots that meet the criteria at the intersection of:
      1. arterial or collector and local roads; and,
      2. two local roads.
    3. Prepare draft Official Plan policies and a zoning by-law amendment, as necessary, to support the implementation of five or more residential units per lot; and
    4. Report back to Council in 2027 with findings, proposed policy directions, and recommended regulatory changes for consideration.

motions.item_title: Exploring the Potential for Five Plus (5+) Units in Guelph, 2026-229
motions.name: Second Motion
motions.text: That staff be directed to take no further action in regard to the five plus units project on low density residential lots, at this time, and continue to monitor the uptake for four units through the annual Guelph Growth Management Report; That the remaining budget allocated to this project from the Housing Accelerator Fund be redirected to other projects that are Housing Accelerator Fund funded.
motions.text_html:
1. That staff be directed to take no further action in regard to the five plus units project on low density residential lots, at this time, and continue to monitor the uptake for four units through the annual Guelph Growth Management Report;
  2. That the remaining budget allocated to this project from the Housing Accelerator Fund be redirected to other projects that are Housing Accelerator Fund funded.
